items.title: 声明宏：模式与重复
items.summary: 用有限模式匹配消除重复；expr、ident、tt 捕获在模板明确类型槽拒绝，完整捕获表达式保持调用点类型。
items.usage: values!(next(), next(), 9) 构造列表，两个 next 各调用一次。twice 示例显式保存参数，避免重复求值。
items.limitation: 模板重复写两次表达式就可能求值两次；不是自动惰性或完整 hygiene。没有 type 片段；歧义转换/单实参泛型不在本轮类别判断范围。过程宏与外部预编译宏包未交付。

items.title: 封闭 enum 与明确状态
items.summary: 用具名变体表示状态与载荷，避免将任意整数当成有效状态。
items.usage: State::Count(3) 与 State::Empty 具有同一个封闭名义类型。每个变体使用独立的内联载荷槽；普通赋值按 Go 的浅值复制规则复制它们。非法原生 Go 表示在已覆盖的使用点校验。
items.limitation: 直接递归值布局须通过指针或容器间接层打断；slice、map、pointer 等载荷仍保留普通 Go 浅复制语义。不支持开放 raw/C enum，也不承诺所有公开函数入口都校验完整对象图。用户泛型 enum 尚不可用。

items.title: match、guard 与表达式
items.summary: 穷尽匹配配合 guard，把分支结果作为值使用。
items.usage: 正数 Count 匹配 guard，其余 Count 和 Empty 提供后备分支。scrutinee 不重复求值。值模式复制载荷；ref / ref mut 显式绑定原始槽，match &value / match &mut value 设置默认绑定。
items.limitation: guard 不代替穷尽覆盖。借用模式保留入口判别快照与固定载荷槽；guard 修改 owner 不会重新选择变体。引用元素及 Go 桥接仍受现有类型权限约束，不代表完整借用检查。

items.title: Option / Result 与 ?
items.summary: 显式表达缺失与失败；? 向最近的用户函数传播，并可使用已登记的单步错误转换。
items.usage: 返回类型和 match 目标提供上下文，可写 Result::Ok/Err、Option::Some/None；nextPort 仍在失败时用登记的 From 单步转换。
items.limitation: 没有通用 Try/Residual、转换链搜索或全程序联合推导。缺少直接期望类型的 None、Result 单侧构造须补显式参数；不会从后续 return 反推局部变量。

items.title: Go 返回值适配：静态 T/E 推导
items.summary: go_result! / go_result_keep! 是编译器保留 builtin，无须 use 宏，不是 std 导出宏。编译器生成适配与载荷检查，std/sum 提供共享 Result 类型和构造器。
items.usage: 用 use 绑定原生 Go 包；显式适配只求值原调用一次。Atoi 失败时普通版丢弃 int；Reader 返回 n>0 与 EOF 时，keep 版保留 Value 和原 Err。? 沿用可赋值优先、精确一步 From 的错误传播，不自动丢弃 partial value。
items.limitation: 只接收一个返回 E 或 (T,E) 的调用；兼容 (T,call) 形式要求两个结果且 T 完全相同。E 须实现 error 且可为 nil，按原静态 E 判断：nil 指针可成功，接口内 typed nil 仍失败。T/E 须在包作用域可命名；保值不是 Clone，多成功值先组合。普通 .go 不支持这些宏或 ?；没有 std.go_result! 限定入口。

items.title: PartialEq / Eq 与 Clone
items.summary: 显式派生资格，使用 .equals 做内容比较；Clone 不改变普通赋值。
items.usage: Batch 的 slice 克隆后可独立改动；修改前 equals 为 true，改后为 false。
items.limitation: 不自动为 pointer/interface 任意载荷提供 Clone/比较协议，不承诺循环容器图比较或全局深拷贝。

items.title: Default、Debug 与格式宏
items.summary: 具体类型可显式派生或登记 Default；Debug 和固定格式宏让输出可读。
items.usage: DefaultSettings() 返回端口 8080；普通 var 的零值仍为 0。println!("{:?}", value) 使用登记的 Debug。
items.limitation: 完整 trait、手写 Clone/Debug 登记与递归 Default 资格仍有限。占位符数量不匹配会拒绝。

items.title: serde 核心协议与 JSON
items.summary: serde::Serialize / serde::Deserialize 由当前文件 use 的 serde 协议拥有者解析；JSON 是独立格式实现。
items.usage: use serde; 后可派生 serde::Serialize 和 serde::Deserialize；别名与直接项 use 保留真实 owner。Config 用 serde::json 生成 JSON；Request.Limit 的缺失与 null 都解为 None。
items.limitation: Option 不代表 PATCH 的 missing/null/value 三态。Option[chan int] 缺少协议会拒绝；字段 adapter、自动 MarshalJSON、JSON Value 与 YAML 不能按提案当作现有 API。

items.title: Error 派生与错误链
items.summary: 显式 Error / #[from] 将业务错误、单步转换和 Go errors.Is/As 连起来。
items.usage: PortError 包装解析错误；errors.Is 仍识别 strconv.ErrSyntax，错误链无需压成字符串。
items.limitation: 已传入的 cause 可以保留；不凭错误文案重建底层错误身份，也不自动生成任意 From 转换。

items.title: use / pub use 与 API 聚合
items.summary: 从显式项目依赖根 use 包或公开项；pub use 重导出公开项，保留变量存储与宏定义点。
items.usage: 公开工程快照中 Counter 与 impl::Count 指向同一存储；源图宏通过 facade 使用。
items.limitation: 跨包源码图与外部宏需要 CLI 工程；Playground 只接受固定依赖上下文和一个用户包，未声明根会拒绝。

snippet.note: 下方 CLI 工程快照可查看实际源码、生成 Go 与输出。片段不能单独放进 Playground。

items.title: feature、依赖来源与 targets
items.summary: format 2 的 goxide.toml 统一 module、原生 Go 依赖政策、增强依赖、feature 与目标；goxide.lock 固定真实解析结果。
items.usage: 最小工程根只有 TOML 和源码：默认 pretty=true，关闭默认 feature 后 false。Go module 元数据只进入受管 target；锁记录真实选版和校验，不将历史 go.sum 当版本列表。 已有 go.mod 的 CLI 单文件按输入最近祖先 module 恢复已登记外部 enum/协议，在同一图中 build/run；只编译指定文件。
items.limitation: TOML 作者根与 go.mod/go.sum 或旧 hgo.lock 并存会拒绝；无 TOML 的原生 Go 依赖仍受支持。offline 通常需要缓存，不冻结本地 path。原生 vendor 只作输入，物化普通本地模块；go.work 使用显式迁入模式，旧 format 不自动升级。 单文件不隐选 TOML/workspace target/features；不可导入的 internal-origin 增强操作仍拒绝，浏览器不解析任意 module。

snippet.text:
[package]
format = 2
module = "example.org/catalog"
go = "1.27"

[features]
default = ["pretty"]
pretty = []

[[bin]]
name = "demo"
path = "src/main.gox"
snippet.note: 仅此清单是作者配置；实际 goxide.lock 与两种运行输出见工程快照。target 内生成 Go 元数据。

items.title: 从普通 Go 迁入：plan → 新目录
items.summary: import-go 先只读输出候选 TOML，再在全新目录 staging 构建显式目标，成功才发布目的工程。
items.usage: 下方最小例从 main.go/go.mod 生成 format 2 TOML 与 schema 2 锁，原文件哈希不变；新目录首次 offline+locked 运行得到同一输出。
items.limitation: 仅接受未迁入的普通 Go module，不自动升级旧 format/JSON/增强锁。不覆盖现有目录；go.work 需显式 --workspace；未支持指令拒绝。原生 module vendor 的受限迁入见独立条目。不执行用户程序、go generate 或脚本；示例运行是单独验证步骤。

snippet.text:
goxide import-go --plan --bin app=. old-project
goxide import-go --out new-project --bin app=. --offline old-project
goxide run --bin app --offline --locked new-project
snippet.note: 命令由本地构建过程执行并留下快照；浏览器不会执行迁移、构建或运行 Go。

items.title: 宿主构建脚本与授权
items.summary: 已选 manifest 输入/输出与脚本身份参与可信构建、缓存和目标隔离。
items.usage: 已知构建脚本可以从 schema 生成 Go/数据；只有精确授权的脚本、helper、依赖和工具才可执行。
items.limitation: 这是非沙箱本机程序；offline 不禁止脚本联网。网页不运行脚本，也不请求用户给予构建权限。 TOML 与新锁不代替授权；生成前仍先检查图与配置。

snippet.note: 选自已验证的 schema 生成工程；不是独立可运行工程。TOML/锁迁移不会授予脚本执行权。

items.title: 只读路径与写引用
items.summary: &T 与 &mut T 保留访问权限；引用可复制、保存、返回和捕获，并可指向同一存储。
items.usage: ref value / ref mut value 绑定原始 enum 载荷槽；match &value / match &mut value 设置默认绑定模式。示例返回并保存载荷引用，修改原值时普通 enum 副本保持独立。
items.limitation: 只读不是全局不可变，可写引用不承诺独占。替换 enum 后，旧引用仍指向原来的固定槽；它不跟随当前变体，写入非活跃槽也不切换变体。没有新增生命周期或借用风险检查器。

items.title: 别名与借用风险分析
items.summary: 已确认独立长期方向，未纳入当前编译器的完整风险分析器。
items.usage: 设计用途：在有具体证据时提示别名留存或重入风险；类型权限检查与可选风险诊断分层。
items.limitation: 不能宣称 Rust 借用安全或因为无法证明独占就默认拒绝。没有该能力的 Playground 入口。

items.title: 静态协议、关联函数与 impl
items.summary: 显式 trait / impl 支持返回 Self 的关联函数；具体类型与协议约束泛型参数都可用静态路径调用。
items.usage: 用 trait Build 声明 Abc() Self，再为 User 编写 impl。User::Abc() 与 Make[T Build] 中的 T::Abc() 调用对应实现；同包多文件示例将协议和实现分开。
items.limitation: 当前是具有限定语法的静态协议切片，不包括关联类型、动态 trait 对象、declare impl、完整固有 impl 或完整 RFC 泛型能力。浏览器只编辑一个包，不加载任意跨模块协议产物。

items.title: safe std、锁与集合
items.summary: 方向是围绕真实 Go 契约逐 API 提供包装；此处是设计范围，不是已发布的库 API。
items.usage: 设计用途：锁回调明确访问与释放；集合视图区分复制和别名；I/O 包装保留部分成功。
items.limitation: 现有 Go slice/map 与可调用的标准包不等于 safe Vec/Map/Lock/Arc 已交付。候选名称、完整桥接与库版本不能当作安装指引。

items.title: quote / syn 与过程宏
items.summary: quote / syn 作为额外语法工具包是已确认目标；用户过程宏延期。
items.usage: 设计用途：读取或构造带来源的语法数据，再交给语义检查；解析成功不代表类型正确。
items.limitation: 公共 API、token 协议与首版范围尚未冻结；当前 macro_rules! 不是运行任意用户 AST 程序的宿主。

items.title: 降低约束与公开边界
items.summary: 真实生成 Go 需要保持求值、控制流、类型身份和已覆盖的权限规则。
items.usage: 目录里的 Go 全部由当前 CLI 产生；浏览器同例逐字节对照，CLI 工程单独运行。
items.limitation: 测试证明列出的子集，不能推导全部组合完成；源码映射、公开入口及不可命名外部载荷仍存在限制。

items.title: 显式依赖根与静态路径
items.summary: use 从项目显式声明的依赖根选择包或公开项；静态包、类型、宏和派生路径使用 ::，值成员使用 .。
items.usage: use serde::json as json; 绑定明确命名空间，json::Marshal 调用包项；item.Value 访问值字段。Playground 展示并验证同一 CLI/WASM 依赖根配置。
items.limitation: 不接受 .gox 的旧 import、包成员点号或字符串 use 路径；不会猜测模块根或扫描目录。依赖映射不下载模块、激活 feature 或授权脚本。

snippet.note: Playground 的固定项目声明在下方依赖源码视图展示。包静态路径与值成员使用不同分隔符。

items.development: 本轮实现显式项目依赖根、use 绑定与 :: 静态路径；支持范围以当前源码、CLI/WASM 定向验收和下方限制为准。

items.title: 分仓标准库与编译器支持
items.summary: 公开 std 提供共享 Option/Result 身份、格式化与运行时支持，以及静态协议的零值类型载体；serde core / JSON 独立分层。
items.usage: 生成 Go 导入 std/sum、std/formatting、std/runtime 或 std/typeinfo，不依赖编译器支持包。typeinfo::Of 提取零值载体，不构造目标 T 或运行锚点方法；具体载荷 validator 仍由编译器生成。JSON 使用独立 serde/json。
items.limitation: enum schema 9 / reference 3 / use 3 / sum ABI 3 / protocol metadata 1 / typeinfo ABI 1 必须与配套 std 版本共同使用。旧 interface case API 已删除，旧产物须重生成。Option 零值为 None，Result 零值非法。固定版本不等于 v1 ABI 承诺。

items.title: 上下文推导与生成 Go 可读性
items.summary: 明确上下文下的 Option:: / Result:: 构造和 pattern 可省泛型参数；部分私有辅助代码已简化。
items.usage: 本页 result 例直接展示 return 和 match 的省参写法。私有 validator 使用较短稳定名，纯空载荷 switch 被省略；完整限定且无 guard 的 match 可用 else-if。
items.limitation: 无上下文构造仍拒绝，不做跨语句反推。guard/推导 match 与有效载荷检查仍保留必要辅助逻辑，公开完整摘要不缩短；可读性改善不等于性能提升。

items.title: CLI：明确的长短选项与参数边界
items.summary: Cobra 命令树提供中文 help、四种 shell completion 与 scripts 六个动作子命令。业务入口使用独立 typed request/service。
items.usage: 长选项使用 --name，短选项使用 -x；选项放在输入之前。run INPUT -- ARGS 保留程序参数，其他命令不开放任意透传。 语言名Goxide，命令goxide，源码.gox，环境变量GOXIDE_*；旧.hgo/HGO_*输入拒绝。
items.limitation: 拒绝旧 Go 风格 -go / -offline 并提示迁移；仅支持已定义的短选项组合，不承诺全部 POSIX 规则。help/completion 不运行构建、下载或脚本。

snippet.text:
goxide run --offline --locked project -- --name value
goxide scripts --help
goxide completion bash
snippet.note: 浏览器不执行 CLI；下方快照来自构建时真实验证。

items.title: 供应模块：local 默认与显式 remote 选择
items.summary: vendor仅作Go迁移输入，没有长期vendor构建模式；默认将供应字节物化普通本地模块，也可明确选择有证据的精确Go module远端来源。
items.usage: stdin/stderr都为TTY且无source参数时，一次展示模块清单；空行全部local，cancel/EOF取消。非TTY默认local且不读管道；重复--source MODULE=local|remote显式选择。差异逐文件列出，TTY需逐模块输入remote MODULE，非TTY需--accept-source-diff MODULE；原供应字节始终保留。
items.limitation: remote仅限原清单证实的精确module path/version（含版本化replacement），local replacement不能确认remote。无Git推断、任意URL、新版本搜索或registry。verified subset只证明供应文件集合相同；unknown不可冒称全发行物等价。--offline禁止工具控制的网络，暖完整缓存可核验remote，缺缓存失败；不隔离用户脚本网络。plan不读取终端、不比对remote，常规build不询问。

snippet.text:
goxide import-go --out new-project --bin app=. --offline --source example.org/d=remote --accept-source-diff example.org/d old-project
goxide run --bin app --offline --locked new-project
snippet.note: 示例候选来自原清单；offline remote要求完整缓存。下方真实CLI快照展示差异拒绝/确认和原字节保留；浏览器不执行迁入或网络请求。

items.title: Workspace：作者核心与统一根锁
items.summary: 作者 workspace 核心已实现：显式继承、全 workspace 统一版本与根唯一 schema 3 锁；仅所选成员及活动依赖参与编译。
items.usage: 成员须显式 package1 = { workspace = true } 才继承模板。全体成员政策参与版本求解，选中构建另合并 feature；--package 选择成员，--bin / --example 选择命名目标。复制根锁拆出可复用可达版本与 Git pin。
items.limitation: 成员/import 不自动建边或覆盖来源。复制锁不复制 path 源码，继承须物化；首次锁定可能取未选依赖元数据，不运行脚本。原生go.work迁入有独立schema4模式；统一host resolver、细粒度lock update、publish/registry尚未实现。批量构建不是事务性发布。

snippet.text:
goxide run --package example.org/service --bin web workspace
goxide run --package example.org/service --example hello workspace
goxide build --workspace --offline --locked workspace
snippet.note: 下面的真实工程快照展示统一选版、feature恢复及复制根锁拆出；不能放进单文件Playground。

items.title: go.work 迁入与本地模块渐进增强
items.summary: 只读plan后向新目录迁入，保留成员go/require/replace/exclude/godebug与根work政策；真实Go包归属分析物化显式成员边，根schema4锁与作者模式schema3分开。
items.usage: 迁入后可逐步加入.gox、现有features与明确授权的scripts；未授权不执行，撤销后缓存也拒绝。成员拆出显式物化继承/path并复制根锁，只消费可达记录，恢复成员独立政策。 供应模块来源选择与单模块一致，显式 remote 按普通 Go replacement/锁验证。
items.limitation: 分析限迁入时平台、Go工具与C配置，换配置需重新分析。供应vendor保留字节/权限，不下载补包或重建；供应源码是普通本地模块，没有vendor构建/拆出模式，独立时物化路径并复制根锁。外部非成员replace不自动打包；不承诺全部workspace功能、统一host resolver或publish。

snippet.text:
goxide import-go --workspace --plan --offline native
goxide import-go --workspace --out migrated --offline native
goxide run --package example.org/app --locked --offline migrated
snippet.note: offline只使用本地材料和完整缓存，remote缺缓存失败；所有来源选择受同一规则约束。脚本仍需明确授权，网页不执行迁入。

/*
Package fmt implements formatted I/O with functions analogous
to C's printf and scanf.  The format 'verbs' are derived from C's but
are simpler.

# Printing

There are four families of printing functions defined by their output destination.
[Print], [Println] and [Printf] write to [os.Stdout];
[Sprint], [Sprintln] and [Sprintf] return a string;
[Fprint], [Fprintln] and [Fprintf] write to an [io.Writer]; and
[Append], [Appendln] and [Appendf] append the output to a byte slice.

The functions within each family do the formatting according to the end of the name.
Print, Sprint, Fprint and Append use the default format for each argument,
adding a space between operands when neither is a string.
Println, Sprintln, Fprintln and Appendln always add spaces and append a newline.
Printf, Sprintf, Fprintf and Appendf use a sequence of "verbs" to control the formatting.

The verbs:

General:

	%v	the value in a default format
		when printing structs, the plus flag (%+v) adds field names
	%#v	a Go-syntax representation of the value
		(floating-point infinities and NaNs print as ±Inf and NaN)
	%T	a Go-syntax representation of the type of the value
	%%	a literal percent sign; consumes no value

Boolean:

	%t	the word true or false

Integer:

	%b	base 2
	%c	the character represented by the corresponding Unicode code point
	%d	base 10
	%o	base 8
	%O	base 8 with 0o prefix
	%q	a single-quoted rune literal safely escaped with Go syntax.
	%x	base 16, with lower-case letters for a-f
	%X	base 16, with upper-case letters for A-F
	%U	Unicode format: U+1234; same as "U+%04X"

Floating-point and complex constituents:

	%b	decimalless scientific notation with exponent a power of two,
		in the manner of strconv.FormatFloat with the 'b' format,
		e.g. -123456p-78
	%e	scientific notation, e.g. -1.234456e+78
	%E	scientific notation, e.g. -1.234456E+78
	%f	decimal point but no exponent, e.g. 123.456
	%F	synonym for %f
	%g	%e for large exponents, %f otherwise. Precision is discussed below.
	%G	%E for large exponents, %F otherwise
	%x	hexadecimal notation (with decimal power of two exponent), e.g. -0x1.23abcp+20
	%X	upper-case hexadecimal notation, e.g. -0X1.23ABCP+20

	The exponent is always a decimal integer.
	For formats other than %b the exponent is at least two digits.

String and slice of bytes (treated equivalently with these verbs):

	%s	the uninterpreted bytes of the string or slice
	%q	a double-quoted string safely escaped with Go syntax
	%x	base 16, lower-case, two characters per byte
	%X	base 16, upper-case, two characters per byte

Slice:

	%p	address of 0th element in base 16 notation, with leading 0x

Pointer:

	%p	base 16 notation, with leading 0x
	The %b, %d, %o, %x and %X verbs also work with pointers,
	formatting the value exactly as if it were an integer.

The default format for %v is:

	bool:                    %t
	int, int8 etc.:          %d
	uint, uint8 etc.:        %d, %#x if printed with %#v
	float32, complex64, etc: %g
	string:                  %s
	chan:                    %p
	pointer:                 %p

For compound objects, the elements are printed using these rules, recursively,
laid out like this:

	struct:             {field0 field1 ...}
	array, slice:       [elem0 elem1 ...]
	maps:               map[key1:value1 key2:value2 ...]
	pointer to above:   &{}, &[], &map[]

Width is specified by an optional decimal number immediately preceding the verb.
If absent, the width is whatever is necessary to represent the value.
Precision is specified after the (optional) width by a period followed by a
decimal number. If no period is present, a default precision is used.
A period with no following number specifies a precision of zero.
Examples:

	%f     default width, default precision
	%9f    width 9, default precision
	%.2f   default width, precision 2
	%9.2f  width 9, precision 2
	%9.f   width 9, precision 0

Width and precision are measured in units of Unicode code points,
that is, runes. (This differs from C's printf where the
units are always measured in bytes.) Either or both of the flags
may be replaced with the character '*', causing their values to be
obtained from the next operand (preceding the one to format),
which must be of type int.

For most values, width is the minimum number of runes to output,
padding the formatted form with spaces if necessary.

For strings, byte slices and byte arrays, however, precision
limits the length of the input to be formatted (not the size of
the output), truncating if necessary. Normally it is measured in
runes, but for these types when formatted with the %x or %X format
it is measured in bytes.

For floating-point values, width sets the minimum width of the field and
precision sets the number of places after the decimal, if appropriate,
except that for %g/%G precision sets the maximum number of significant
digits (trailing zeros are removed). For example, given 12.345 the format
%6.3f prints 12.345 while %.3g prints 12.3. The default precision for %e, %f
and %#g is 6; for %g it is the smallest number of digits necessary to identify
the value uniquely.

For complex numbers, the width and precision apply to the two
components independently and the result is parenthesized, so %f applied
to 1.2+3.4i produces (1.200000+3.400000i).

When formatting a single integer code point or a rune string (type []rune)
with %q, invalid Unicode code points are changed to the Unicode replacement
character, U+FFFD, as in [strconv.QuoteRune].

Other flags:

	'+'	always print a sign for numeric values;
		guarantee ASCII-only output for %q (%+q)
	'-'	pad with spaces on the right rather than the left (left-justify the field)
	'#'	alternate format: add leading 0b for binary (%#b), 0 for octal (%#o),
		0x or 0X for hex (%#x or %#X); suppress 0x for %p (%#p);
		for %q, print a raw (backquoted) string if [strconv.CanBackquote]
		returns true;
		always print a decimal point for %e, %E, %f, %F, %g and %G;
		do not remove trailing zeros for %g and %G;
		write e.g. U+0078 'x' if the character is printable for %U (%#U)
	' '	(space) leave a space for elided sign in numbers (% d);
		put spaces between bytes printing strings or slices in hex (% x, % X)
	'0'	pad with leading zeros rather than spaces;
		for numbers, this moves the padding after the sign

Flags are ignored by verbs that do not expect them.
For example there is no alternate decimal format, so %#d and %d
behave identically.

For each Printf-like function, there is also a Print function
that takes no format and is equivalent to saying %v for every
operand.  Another variant Println inserts blanks between
operands and appends a newline.

Regardless of the verb, if an operand is an interface value,
the internal concrete value is used, not the interface itself.
Thus:

	var i interface{} = 23
	fmt.Printf("%v\n", i)

will print 23.

Except when printed using the verbs %T and %p, special
formatting considerations apply for operands that implement
certain interfaces. In order of application:

1. If the operand is a [reflect.Value], the operand is replaced by the
concrete value that it holds, and printing continues with the next rule.

2. If an operand implements the [Formatter] interface, it will
be invoked. In this case the interpretation of verbs and flags is
controlled by that implementation.

3. If the %v verb is used with the # flag (%#v) and the operand
implements the [GoStringer] interface, that will be invoked.

If the format (which is implicitly %v for [Println] etc.) is valid
for a string (%s %q %x %X), or is %v but not %#v,
the following two rules apply:

4. If an operand implements the error interface, the Error method
will be invoked to convert the object to a string, which will then
be formatted as required by the verb (if any).

5. If an operand implements method String() string, that method
will be invoked to convert the object to a string, which will then
be formatted as required by the verb (if any).

For compound operands such as slices and structs, the format
applies to the elements of each operand, recursively, not to the
operand as a whole. Thus %q will quote each element of a slice
of strings, and %6.2f will control formatting for each element
of a floating-point array.

However, when printing a byte slice with a string-like verb
(%s %q %x %X), it is treated identically to a string, as a single item.

To avoid recursion in cases such as

	type X string
	func (x X) String() string { return Sprintf("<%s>", x) }

convert the value before recurring:

	func (x X) String() string { return Sprintf("<%s>", string(x)) }

Infinite recursion can also be triggered by self-referential data
structures, such as a slice that contains itself as an element, if
that type has a String method. Such pathologies are rare, however,
and the package does not protect against them.

When printing a struct, fmt cannot and therefore does not invoke
formatting methods such as Error or String on unexported fields.

# Explicit argument indexes

In [Printf], [Sprintf], [Fprintf], and [Appendf], the default behavior is for each
formatting verb to format successive arguments passed in the call.
However, the notation [n] immediately before the verb indicates that the
nth one-indexed argument is to be formatted instead. The same notation
before a '*' for a width or precision selects the argument index holding
the value. After processing a bracketed expression [n], subsequent verbs
will use arguments n+1, n+2, etc. unless otherwise directed.

For example,

	fmt.Sprintf("%[2]d %[1]d\n", 11, 22)

will yield "22 11", while

	fmt.Sprintf("%[3]*.[2]*[1]f", 12.0, 2, 6)

equivalent to

	fmt.Sprintf("%6.2f", 12.0)

will yield " 12.00". Because an explicit index affects subsequent verbs,
this notation can be used to print the same values multiple times
by resetting the index for the first argument to be repeated:

	fmt.Sprintf("%d %d %#[1]x %#x", 16, 17)

will yield "16 17 0x10 0x11".

# Format errors

If an invalid argument is given for a verb, such as providing
a string to %d, the generated string will contain a
description of the problem, as in these examples:

	Wrong type or unknown verb: %!verb(type=value)
		Printf("%d", "hi"):        %!d(string=hi)
	Too many arguments: %!(EXTRA type=value)
		Printf("hi", "guys"):      hi%!(EXTRA string=guys)
	Too few arguments: %!verb(MISSING)
		Printf("hi%d"):            hi%!d(MISSING)
	Non-int for width or precision: %!(BADWIDTH) or %!(BADPREC)
		Printf("%*s", 4.5, "hi"):  %!(BADWIDTH)hi
		Printf("%.*s", 4.5, "hi"): %!(BADPREC)hi
	Invalid or invalid use of argument index: %!(BADINDEX)
		Printf("%*[2]d", 7):       %!d(BADINDEX)
		Printf("%.[2]d", 7):       %!d(BADINDEX)

All errors begin with the string "%!" followed sometimes
by a single character (the verb) and end with a parenthesized
description.

If an Error or String method triggers a panic when called by a
print routine, the fmt package reformats the error message
from the panic, decorating it with an indication that it came
through the fmt package.  For example, if a String method
calls panic("bad"), the resulting formatted message will look
like

	%!s(PANIC=bad)

The %!s just shows the print verb in use when the failure
occurred. If the panic is caused by a nil receiver to an Error,
String, or GoString method, however, the output is the undecorated
string, "<nil>".

Many packages whose APIs involve string formatting expose a trio of
functions similar to [Print], [Printf], and [Println].
For example, the [log.Print], [log.Printf] and [log.Println] functions
forward their arguments to the corresponding functions in this package.
To avoid confusion, other wrapper functions should follow the naming
and behavioral conventions established by this package.
In particular, a single function should not choose between literal
printing (like [Print]) and formatted printing (like [Printf])
based on the number of arguments; instead, provide separate functions.

# Scanning

An analogous set of functions scans formatted text to yield
values.  [Scan], [Scanf] and [Scanln] read from [os.Stdin]; [Fscan],
[Fscanf] and [Fscanln] read from a specified [io.Reader]; [Sscan],
[Sscanf] and [Sscanln] read from an argument string.

[Scan], [Fscan], [Sscan] treat newlines in the input as spaces.

[Scanln], [Fscanln] and [Sscanln] stop scanning at a newline and
require that the items be followed by a newline or EOF.

[Scanf], [Fscanf], and [Sscanf] parse the arguments according to a
format string, analogous to that of [Printf]. In the text that
follows, 'space' means any Unicode whitespace character
except newline.

In the format string, a verb introduced by the % character
consumes and parses input; these verbs are described in more
detail below. A character other than %, space, or newline in
the format consumes exactly that input character, which must
be present. A newline with zero or more spaces before it in
the format string consumes zero or more spaces in the input
followed by a single newline or the end of the input. A space
following a newline in the format string consumes zero or more
spaces in the input. Otherwise, any run of one or more spaces
in the format string consumes as many spaces as possible in
the input. Unless the run of spaces in the format string
appears adjacent to a newline, the run must consume at least
one space from the input or find the end of the input.

The handling of spaces and newlines differs from that of C's
scanf family: in C, newlines are treated as any other space,
and it is never an error when a run of spaces in the format
string finds no spaces to consume in the input.

The verbs behave analogously to those of [Printf].
For example, %x will scan an integer as a hexadecimal number,
and %v will scan the default representation format for the value.
The [Printf] verbs %p and %T and the flags # and + are not implemented.
For floating-point and complex values, all valid formatting verbs
(%b %e %E %f %F %g %G %x %X and %v) are equivalent and accept
both decimal and hexadecimal notation (for example: "2.3e+7", "0x4.5p-8")
and digit-separating underscores (for example: "3.14159_26535_89793").

Input processed by verbs is implicitly space-delimited: the
implementation of every verb except %c starts by discarding
leading spaces from the remaining input, and the %s verb
(and %v reading into a string) stops consuming input at the first
space or newline character.

The familiar base-setting prefixes 0b (binary), 0o and 0 (octal),
and 0x (hexadecimal) are accepted when scanning integers
without a format or with the %v verb, as are digit-separating
underscores.

Width is interpreted in the input text but there is no
syntax for scanning with a precision (no %5.2f, just %5f).
If width is provided, it applies after leading spaces are
trimmed and specifies the maximum number of runes to read
to satisfy the verb. For example,

	Sscanf(" 1234567 ", "%5s%d", &s, &i)

will set s to "12345" and i to 67 while

	Sscanf(" 12 34 567 ", "%5s%d", &s, &i)

will set s to "12" and i to 34.

In all the scanning functions, a carriage return followed
immediately by a newline is treated as a plain newline
(\r\n means the same as \n).

In all the scanning functions, if an operand implements method
[Scan] (that is, it implements the [Scanner] interface) that
method will be used to scan the text for that operand.  Also,
if the number of arguments scanned is less than the number of
arguments provided, an error is returned.

All arguments to be scanned must be either pointers to basic
types or implementations of the [Scanner] interface.

Like [Scanf] and [Fscanf], [Sscanf] need not consume its entire input.
There is no way to recover how much of the input string [Sscanf] used.

Note: [Fscan] etc. can read one character (rune) past the input
they return, which means that a loop calling a scan routine
may skip some of the input.  This is usually a problem only
when there is no space between input values.  If the reader
provided to [Fscan] implements ReadRune, that method will be used
to read characters.  If the reader also implements UnreadRune,
that method will be used to save the character and successive
calls will not lose data.  To attach ReadRune and UnreadRune
methods to a reader without that capability, use
[bufio.NewReader].
*/

// Package serde defines format-independent serialization protocols.
package serde

type WriteValue func(Serializer) error
type ReadValue func(Deserializer) error

type Serializer interface {
	Bool(bool) error
	Int64(int64) error
	Uint64(uint64) error
	Float64(float64) error
	String(string) error
	Bytes([]byte) error
	None() error
	Some(WriteValue) error
	Seq(int) (SeqWriter, error)
	Map(int) (MapWriter, error)
	Struct(string, int) (StructWriter, error)
	UnitVariant(string, string) error
	NewtypeVariant(string, string, WriteValue) error
}
type SeqWriter interface {
	Element(WriteValue) error
	End() error
}
type MapWriter interface {
	Entry(WriteValue, WriteValue) error
	End() error
}
type StructWriter interface {
	Field(string, WriteValue) error
	End() error
}

type Deserializer interface {
	Bool(Visitor) error
	Int64(Visitor) error
	Uint64(Visitor) error
	Float64(Visitor) error
	String(Visitor) error
	Bytes(Visitor) error
	Option(Visitor) error
	Seq(Visitor) error
	Map(Visitor) error
	Struct(string, []string, Visitor) error
	Enum(string, []string, Visitor) error
	Any(Visitor) error
	Skip() error
}
type Visitor interface {
	VisitBool(bool) error
	VisitInt64(int64) error
	VisitUint64(uint64) error
	VisitFloat64(float64) error
	VisitString(string) error
	VisitBytes([]byte) error
	VisitNone() error
	VisitSome(Deserializer) error
	VisitSeq(SeqAccess) error
	VisitMap(MapAccess) error
	VisitEnum(EnumAccess) error
}
type SeqAccess interface{ NextElement(ReadValue) (bool, error) }
type MapAccess interface {
	NextKey(ReadValue) (bool, error)
	NextValue(ReadValue) error
}
type EnumAccess interface {
	Variant() (string, VariantAccess, error)
}
type VariantAccess interface {
	Unit() error
	Newtype(ReadValue) error
}

package = "errors"

package = "io"

package = "strings"

package = "math"

source = "toolchain"
namespaces = { json = "encoding/json" }

module = "github.com/goxide-lang/std"
namespaces = { runtime = "github.com/goxide-lang/std/runtime", formatting = "github.com/goxide-lang/std/formatting", sum = "github.com/goxide-lang/std/sum", typeinfo = "github.com/goxide-lang/std/typeinfo" }

package = "github.com/goxide-lang/serde"
namespaces = { json = "github.com/goxide-lang/serde/json" }
